newsitem.title: USA: Congress campaign spending leaps to new record.
newsitem.headline: Congress campaign spending leaps to new record.

text.p: Congressional campaign spending soared to a record $626.4 million in the 1996 general election, the Federal Election Commission said Tuesday.
This was an increase of $36.8 million or 6.3 percent over the 1994 record level, the FEC said. It said House races accounted for the increase.
A new push for campaign finance reform legislation is expected to be made in the new Congress that convenes January 7 but its prospects are unclear.
The FEC said the total represented only direct spending by candidates' campaigns and did not include spending by parties and other organisations.

It said congressional candidates raised a record $659.6 million, up 8 percent from the $611.5 million raised in 1994. Contributions by political action committees and other committees increased 13 percent from the 1994 level of $169.5 million, while individual contributions increased 14 percent, from $335.7 million to $381.6 million.

The FEC report said House candidates were responsible for the increased spending and fund-raising while Senate figures declined, partly because Senate races were concentrated in states with small populations.

Top spender among Senate candidates was Virginia Democrat Mark Warner who spent $11,504,498 in his losing race against Republican Sen. John Warner. He was closely followed by Massachusetts Democratic Sen. John Kerry, with $10,670,383.
In the House, Republican Speaker Newt Gingrich of Georgia led the spenders with $5,435,744. Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt of Missouri spent $2,925,330.
